sections.heading: How to Play Arms Warrior
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Arms Warrior"][color=warrior]Arms Warrior Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
[tr][td]
Arms Warriors revolve around using abilities to increase the damage of their attacks, inflict bleeds, and maximize Execute damage. Although the standard rotation is not very complex, there are several synergistic talents that create more complex priorities.

[hr]
[table]
[tr]
[td width=7%][icon name=ability_warrior_charge size=medium type=round color=c1 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=warrior]Avoid Downtime[/color][/b] - Arms generates the majority of its rage from auto-attacks, so reducing the amount of time spent chasing, running out mechanics, or otherwise not hitting the boss is critical to maximizing performance. There are several abilities to help with this, such as [spell=100] and [spell=6544], so use them smartly to stay on target as much as possible![/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[hr]
	[table]
	[tr]
[td width=7%][icon name=ability_warrior_savageblow size=medium type=round color=c1 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=warrior]Keep Abilities on cooldown[/color][/b] - Arms generates and spends resources in small amounts, but its ability cooldowns are what really drive the rotation. Keeping Colossus Smash, Avatar, and Bladestorm/Demolish on cooldown is crucial, as delaying any one of them can easily cause the others to desync as well, so avoid doing it without good reason - such as a quickly approaching add or increased damage phase.[/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[hr]
	[table]
	[tr]
[td width=7%][icon name=ability_racial_bloodrage size=medium type=round color=c1 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=warrior]Avoid wasting Rage[/color][/b] - Unlike most resources, Rage starts from zero and decays out of combat. Making efficient use of it will help maintain the rotation and eliminate downtime spent waiting for more resources, both in combat and by reducing the amount of time spent moving from one combat to another.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/td][/tr][/table][/center]
[hr]
[b]Reading Priority Lists[/b]
Abilities and talents are listed from highest to lowest priority in the Arms Warrior rotation. Every time an ability is cast, begin again at the top of the list and move down until there is something that can be cast, then return to the top once more.
[/box][/wrapper][pad]
[center][cta-button=guide=33100 icon=classicon_warrior]Arms Warrior Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Rotation Priority" type=bar][icon name=ability_warrior_challange type=round inline=true size=medium color=c1][/icon] Best Arms Warrior Rotation[/h2]

For all forms of content, Arms follows a priority list of what spells to cast. Below, we break down the main priority lists for Arms Warriors: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and various openers.

[ul][li][b]New in Patch 12.1[/b]: Mortal Strike no longer reduces the cooldown of Demolish and Slayer gains significantly more Sudden Death procs.[/li][/ul]

sections.heading: Opener
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Opener" type=bar][icon name=ability_warrior_charge type=round inline=true size=medium color=c1][/icon] Best Arms Warrior Opener[/h2]

Aside from always opening with [spell=100] for a small boost to rage generation, the Arms opener is virtually identical to its single-target priority.

Unless there are upcoming adds or an increased damage phase, [url=item=133300]stat increasing trinkets[/url] are best used on the pull, while [url=item=212265]combat potions[/url] are better saved for Execute unless two potions will be available during the encounter.

[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Check[/h2]
Before any form of combat, whether raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content, ensure that [spell=6673] is active on yourself and all relevant party members. In higher-end content, applying a food buff, flask, weapon oils, and preparing a combat potion is also a good idea.

sections.heading: Cooldown Usage
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Cooldown Usage" type=bar][icon name=ability_warrior_savageblow type=round inline=true size=medium color=c1][/icon] Arms Warriors Major Cooldowns[/h2]

[pad][pad]

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Colossus Smash" icon=inv_warbreaker]
Arms' primary cooldown should be used liberally whether facing single or multiple targets. Its cooldown is reduced by [spell=152278], which should keep it aligned with Avatar most of the time. Keeping it active as much as possible is perhaps the most important part of maximizing Arms damage.
[/tab]

[tab name="Avatar" icon=warrior_talent_icon_avatar]
A secondary cooldown, it now provides only a basic damage bonus, which should be used with Colossus Smash as much as possible, but is otherwise uneventful.
[/tab]

[tab name="Bladestorm" icon=ability_warrior_bladestorm]
A secondary cooldown used exclusively by Slayer, it deals a good amount of single and multitarget damage, while also triggering supplementary effects such as [spell=1270717] and [spell=386628]. It has a unique form of cooldown reduction, so it will not always align with other cooldowns, making it important to think about when to use the cooldown and when to save it.
[/tab]

[tab name="Champion's Spear" icon=inv_ability_warrior_championsspear]
A talented attack in the class tree, which serves more of a utility role in keeping enemies within an area, though its damage is rather mediocre. The ability can be reactivated to leap to the spear, though this has very niche applications.
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=warrior][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c1][/icon] Arms Warrior Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]

[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Maximizing Uptime"]
Arms Warriors are very straightforward damage dealers, with a very flat damage profile not concentrated entirely into cooldown windows. Because of this, the biggest optimization is simply maximizing uptime on the target - knowing what mechanics are coming [i]before[/i] they actually happen will help plan movement to minimize time spent off target, allowing more rage to be generated and more GCDs to be fit into the overall rotation.

There are a variety of tools to help with this, from using [spell=6544] to move out of range at the last moment before damage goes out, to using [spell=100] after a target has finished moving, which are largely a byproduct of time and experience.
[/tab]
[tab name="Aligning Cooldowns"]
Arms Warriors have several cooldowns, but they're all used more or less the same way - on cooldown as much as possible. When situations or timers allow, cooldowns can be aligned, but they should not be delayed by a significant amount (typically no less than 10-15% of their actual cooldown) unless the delay will allow them to hit multiple targets when they would otherwise hit one, or it will be your final use of the cooldown before the end of the fight regardless.

The reason is that losing an entire use of a cooldown is typically a bigger loss than what is gained by stacking the cooldown with something else to amplify it. Some cooldowns will always align naturally, though others will not, so anticipating those timers and knowing when adds or important damage phases are coming is key.
[/tab]
[/tabs]
